sanskrit: menakā tridaśeṣv eva tridaśāś cānu menakām mamaivodricyate janma duḥṣanta tava janmataḥ
english: Menakā stands high among the thirty gods, and the thirty gods revere Menakā; my birth excels yours, Duḥṣanta, measured from your birth.

sanskrit: kṣitāv aṭasi rājaṃs tvam antarikṣe carāmy aham āvayor antaraṃ paśya merusarṣapayor iva
english: You roam upon the earth, O king, while I move through the sky — see the distance between us as that between Mount Meru and a mustard seed.

sanskrit: mahendrasya kuberasya yamasya varuṇasya ca bhavanāny anusaṃyāmi prabhāvaṃ paśya me nṛpa
english: I visit the palaces of Mahendra, Kubera, Yama, and Varuṇa — behold my power, O king.

sanskrit: satyaś cāpi pravādo 'yaṃ yaṃ pravakṣyāmi te 'nagha nidarśanārthaṃ na dveṣāt tac chrutvā kṣantum arhasi
english: What I am about to tell you, O sinless one, is a true saying — I speak it as an illustration, not out of hatred; having heard it, you should bear with it patiently.

sanskrit: virūpo yāvad ādarśe nātmanaḥ paśyate mukham manyate tāvad ātmānam anyebhyo rūpavattaram
english: As long as an ugly man does not see his own face in a mirror, he considers himself more handsome than others.

sanskrit: yadā tu mukham ādarśe vikṛtaṃ so 'bhivīkṣate tadetaraṃ vijānāti ātmānaṃ netaraṃ janam
english: But when he looks into the mirror and sees his distorted face, he then knows himself truly — not the other person.

sanskrit: atīva rūpasaṃpanno na kiṃ cid avamanyate atīva jalpan durvāco bhavatīha viheṭhakaḥ
english: One who is supremely gifted in beauty does not belittle anything; but one who talks excessively with harsh words becomes a nuisance in this world.

sanskrit: mūrkho hi jalpatāṃ puṃsāṃ śrutvā vācaḥ śubhāśubhāḥ aśubhaṃ vākyam ādatte purīṣam iva sūkaraḥ
english: A fool, hearing both good and bad words spoken by people, picks up only the bad words — like a pig that picks up filth.

sanskrit: prājñas tu jalpatāṃ puṃsāṃ śrutvā vācaḥ śubhāśubhāḥ guṇavad vākyam ādatte haṃsaḥ kṣīram ivāmbhasaḥ
english: But a wise man, hearing both good and bad words spoken by people, takes only the virtuous word — like a swan that separates milk from water.

sanskrit: anyān parivadan sādhur yathā hi paritapyate tathā parivadann anyāṃs tuṣṭo bhavati durjanaḥ
english: Just as a good person feels anguish when he speaks ill of others, in the same way a wicked person feels delight when he slanders others.

sanskrit: abhivādya yathā vṛddhān santo gacchanti nirvṛtim evaṃ sajjanam ākruśya mūrkho bhavati nirvṛtaḥ
english: Just as the righteous attain peace by respectfully saluting elders, so a fool attains a perverse contentment by reviling good people.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ jīvanty adoṣajñā mūrkhā doṣānudarśinaḥ yatra vācyāḥ paraiḥ santaḥ parān āhus tathāvidhān
english: Fools who see no fault in themselves live happily while perceiving faults in others; wherever the virtuous are to be reproached by others, they call those others just such people.

sanskrit: ato hāsyataraṃ loke kiṃ cid anyan na vidyate yatra durjana ity āha durjanaḥ sajjanaṃ svayam
english: There is nothing more laughable in this world than when a wicked man himself calls a virtuous man wicked.

sanskrit: satyadharmacyutāt puṃsaḥ kruddhād āśīviṣād iva anāstiko 'py udvijate janaḥ kiṃ punar āstikaḥ
english: From a man fallen from truth and righteousness, enraged, like a venomous serpent, even a non-believer shrinks away — how much more so a believer.

sanskrit: svayam utpādya vai putraṃ sadṛśaṃ yo 'vamanyate tasya devāḥ śriyaṃ ghnanti na ca lokān upāśnute
english: Whoever, having himself fathered a son in his own likeness, then disrespects him — the gods destroy his prosperity and he does not enjoy the higher worlds.

sanskrit: kulavaṃśapratiṣṭhāṃ hi pitaraḥ putram abruvan uttamaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ tasmāt putraṃ na saṃtyajet
english: The forefathers declared a son to be the highest support of family and lineage, the foremost of all sacred duties — therefore one should never abandon a son.

sanskrit: svapatnīprabhavān pañca labdhān krītān vivardhitān kṛtān anyāsu cotpannān putrān vai manur abravīt
english: Manu declared five kinds of sons: those born of one's own wife, those received as gifts, those purchased, those raised, those begotten on other women, and those adopted.

sanskrit: dharmakīrtyāvahā nṝṇāṃ manasaḥ prītivardhanāḥ trāyante narakāj jātāḥ putrā dharmaplavāḥ pitṝn
english: Sons bring righteousness and glory to men, they increase the joy of the heart, and — born as rafts of dharma — they rescue their fathers from hell.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ nṛpatiśārdūla na putraṃ tyaktum arhasi ātmānaṃ satyadharmau ca pālayāno mahīpate narendrasiṃha kapaṭaṃ na voḍhuṃ tvam ihārhasi
english: Therefore you, O tiger among kings, lord of the earth, lion among rulers, should not abandon your son; protecting yourself, truth, and righteousness, you should not carry deceit in this world.

sanskrit: varaṃ kūpaśatād vāpī varaṃ vāpīśatāt kratuḥ varaṃ kratuśatāt putraḥ satyaṃ putraśatād varam
english: A reservoir is better than a hundred wells; a sacrifice is better than a hundred reservoirs; a son is better than a hundred sacrifices; truth is better than a hundred sons.

sanskrit: aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam aśvamedhasahasrād dhi satyam eva viśiṣyate
english: If a thousand horse-sacrifices and truth are placed in a balance, truth alone surpasses a thousand horse-sacrifices.

sanskrit: sarvavedādhigamanaṃ sarvatīrthāvagāhanam satyaṃ ca vadato rājan samaṃ vā syān na vā samam
english: Mastering all the Vedas and bathing in all the sacred fords — whether these equal speaking truth, O king, or do not equal it, truth is supreme.

sanskrit: nāsti satyāt paro dharmo na satyād vidyate param na hi tīvrataraṃ kiṃ cid anṛtād iha vidyate
english: There is no dharma higher than truth; there is nothing higher than truth; there is indeed nothing more terrible in this world than falsehood.

sanskrit: rājan satyaṃ paraṃ brahma satyaṃ ca samayaḥ paraḥ mā tyākṣīḥ samayaṃ rājan satyaṃ saṃgatam astu te
english: O king, truth is the supreme Brahman; truth is the highest covenant — do not abandon the covenant, O king; let truth be your companion.

sanskrit: anṛte cet prasaṅgas te śraddadhāsi na cet svayam ātmano hanta gacchāmi tvādṛśe nāsti saṃgatam
english: If you are inclined to falsehood and do not believe in truth yourself, then I am leaving — there is no fellowship with one such as you.

sanskrit: ṛte 'pi tvayi duḥṣanta śailarājāvataṃsakam caturantām imām urvīṃ putro me pālayiṣyati
english: Even without you, Duḥṣanta, my son will protect this four-bounded earth adorned with the king of mountains.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ prātiṣṭhata śakuntalā athāntarikṣe duḥṣantaṃ vāg uvācāśarīriṇī ṛtvikpurohitācāryair mantribhiś cāvṛtaṃ tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken these words, Śakuntalā departed. Then, while Duḥṣanta was surrounded by officiating priests, the chief priest, teachers, and ministers, a disembodied voice spoke to him from the sky.

sanskrit: bhastrā mātā pituḥ putro yena jātaḥ sa eva saḥ bharasva putraṃ duḥṣanta māvamaṃsthāḥ śakuntalām
english: The mother is only the bellows; the son belongs to the father from whom he is born. Maintain your son, Duḥṣanta; do not disrespect Śakuntalā.

sanskrit: retodhāḥ putra unnayati naradeva yamakṣayāt tvaṃ cāsya dhātā garbhasya satyam āha śakuntalā
english: The son of the seed-giver raises him from Yama's realm, O lord of men; and you are indeed the sustainer of this womb — Śakuntalā speaks the truth.

sanskrit: jāyā janayate putram ātmano 'ṅgaṃ dvidhā kṛtam tasmād bharasva duḥṣanta putraṃ śākuntalaṃ nṛpa
english: The wife bears a son — the self divided into two parts. Therefore, O king Duḥṣanta, maintain your son, the son of Śakuntalā.

sanskrit: abhūtir eṣā kas tyajyāj jīvañ jīvantam ātmajam śākuntalaṃ mahātmānaṃ dauḥṣantiṃ bhara paurava
english: This is disgrace — who would abandon a living son while himself alive? Maintain the great-souled Śākuntalā, your son Dauḥṣanti, O Paurava.

sanskrit: bhartavyo 'yaṃ tvayā yasmād asmākaṃ vacanād api tasmād bhavatv ayaṃ nāmnā bharato nāma te sutaḥ
english: Because he is to be maintained by you, and also by our command, therefore let this son of yours be named Bharata — 'he who is to be maintained.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā pauravo rājā vyāhṛtaṃ vai divaukasām purohitam amātyāṃś ca saṃprahṛṣṭo 'bravīd idam
english: Hearing the declaration of the heavenly beings, the Paurava king rejoiced and said this to the chief priest and ministers.

sanskrit: śṛṇvantv etad bhavanto 'sya devadūtasya bhāṣitam aham apy evam evainaṃ jānāmi svayam ātmajam
english: May you all hear the words of this divine messenger — I too recognize him myself as my own son in exactly this way.

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ vacanād eva gṛhṇīyām imam ātmajam bhaved dhi śaṅkā lokasya naivaṃ śuddho bhaved ayam
english: If I had accepted him on her word alone, people would have had doubts, and in that way he would not have been certified as pure.

sanskrit: taṃ viśodhya tadā rājā devadūtena bhārata hṛṣṭaḥ pramuditaś cāpi pratijagrāha taṃ sutam
english: Having thus vindicated him through the divine messenger, O Bhārata, the king, filled with joy and delight, accepted his son.

sanskrit: mūrdhni cainam upāghrāya sasnehaṃ pariṣasvaje sabhājyamāno vipraiś ca stūyamānaś ca bandibhiḥ sa mudaṃ paramāṃ lebhe putrasaṃsparśajāṃ nṛpaḥ
english: He smelled the child's head and embraced him with affection; honored by brahmins and praised by bards, the king experienced the supreme joy born of a son's touch.

sanskrit: tāṃ caiva bhāryāṃ dharmajñaḥ pūjayām āsa dharmataḥ abravīc caiva tāṃ rājā sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: The king, who knew dharma, honored that wife according to righteousness, and then the king spoke these conciliatory words to her.

sanskrit: kṛto lokaparokṣo 'yaṃ saṃbandho vai tvayā saha tasmād etan mayā devi tvacchuddhyarthaṃ vicāritam
english: This union with you was made in secret, away from the world's gaze; therefore, O goddess, I deliberated thus in order to establish your purity.

sanskrit: manyate caiva lokas te strībhāvān mayi saṃgatam putraś cāyaṃ vṛto rājye mayā tasmād vicāritam
english: The world might think, on account of you being a woman, that your union with me was improper, and so I accepted this son into the kingdom only after deliberation.

sanskrit: yac ca kopitayātyarthaṃ tvayokto 'smy apriyaṃ priye praṇayinyā viśālākṣi tat kṣāntaṃ te mayā śubhe
english: And what unpleasant words you, though beloved and devoted to me, spoke to me in great anger — all of that I forgive you, O large-eyed auspicious one.

sanskrit: tām evam uktvā rājarṣir duḥṣanto mahiṣīṃ priyām vāsobhir annapānaiś ca pūjayām āsa bhārata
english: Having spoken thus to her, the royal sage Duḥṣanta honored his beloved queen with garments and food and drink, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: duḥṣantaś ca tato rājā putraṃ śākuntalaṃ tadā bharataṃ nāmataḥ kṛtvā yauvarājye 'bhyaṣecayat
english: Then King Duḥṣanta named his son born of Śakuntalā 'Bharata' and consecrated him as the crown prince.

sanskrit: tasya tat prathitaṃ cakraṃ prāvartata mahātmanaḥ bhāsvaraṃ divyam ajitaṃ lokasaṃnādanaṃ mahat
english: The great-souled Bharata's glorious wheel of conquest began to roll — radiant, divine, unconquered, filling the worlds with its resounding might.

sanskrit: sa vijitya mahīpālāṃś cakāra vaśavartinaḥ cacāra ca satāṃ dharmaṃ prāpa cānuttamaṃ yaśaḥ
english: He conquered the rulers of the earth and made them submissive; he walked the path of the virtuous and attained unsurpassed glory.

sanskrit: sa rājā cakravarty āsīt sārvabhaumaḥ pratāpavān īje ca bahubhir yajñair yathā śakro marutpatiḥ
english: That king became a sovereign emperor of the whole earth, blazing with majesty; he performed many sacrifices just as Śakra, the lord of the Maruts, does.

sanskrit: yājayām āsa taṃ kaṇvo dakṣavad bhūridakṣiṇam śrīmān govitataṃ nāma vājimedham avāpa saḥ yasmin sahasraṃ padmānāṃ kaṇvāya bharato dadau
english: Kaṇva caused him to perform a great horse-sacrifice with lavish fees, like Dakṣa; the illustrious one obtained the horse-sacrifice called Govitata, in which Bharata gave Kaṇva a thousand padmas of gold.

sanskrit: bharatād bhāratī kīrtir yenedaṃ bhārataṃ kulam apare ye ca pūrve ca bhāratā iti viśrutāḥ
english: From Bharata came the glory of the Bharatas, by which this family is called Bhārata; both earlier and later descendants became renowned as Bhāratas.

sanskrit: bharatasyānvavāye hi devakalpā mahaujasaḥ babhūvur brahmakalpāś ca bahavo rājasattamāḥ
english: In the lineage of Bharata there were many foremost kings, equal to the gods in power, equal to Brahman in splendor.

sanskrit: yeṣām aparimeyāni nāmadheyāni sarvaśaḥ teṣāṃ tu te yathāmukhyaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi bhārata mahābhāgān devakalpān satyārjavaparāyaṇān
english: Their names are beyond count in every respect, O Bhārata; of those most fortunate ones, equal to gods, devoted to truth and uprightness, I shall recite them to you in order of their eminence.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prajāpates tu dakṣasya manor vaivasvatasya ca bharatasya kuroḥ pūror ajamīḍhasya cānvaye
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: In the lineage of Dakṣa the Progenitor, Manu Vaivasvata, Bharata, Kuru, Pūru, and Ajamīḍha —

sanskrit: yādavānām imaṃ vaṃśaṃ pauravāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ tathaiva bhāratānāṃ ca puṇyaṃ svastyayanaṃ mahat dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi te 'nagha
english: — this lineage of the Yādavas and that of the Pauravas in full, and likewise of the Bhāratas — holy, conferring welfare, meritorious, glory-giving, life-prolonging — I shall recite to you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tejobhir uditāḥ sarve maharṣisamatejasaḥ daśa pracetasaḥ putrāḥ santaḥ pūrvajanāḥ smṛtāḥ meghajenāgninā ye te pūrvaṃ dagdhā mahaujasaḥ
english: All blazing with splendor equal to great sages, the ten sons of Pracetas are remembered as the primeval beings — those mighty ones who were burnt by the fire born of clouds.

sanskrit: tebhyaḥ prācetaso jajñe dakṣo dakṣād imāḥ prajāḥ saṃbhūtāḥ puruṣavyāghra sa hi lokapitāmahaḥ
english: From those ten was born Dakṣa, son of Pracetas; from Dakṣa, O tiger among men, these creatures came into being — he is indeed the grandfather of all the worlds.

sanskrit: vīriṇyā saha saṃgamya dakṣaḥ prācetaso muniḥ ātmatulyān ajanayat sahasraṃ saṃśitavratān
english: Dakṣa, the sage son of Pracetas, uniting with Vīriṇī, fathered a thousand sons equal to himself, firm in their vows.

sanskrit: sahasrasaṃkhyān samitān sutān dakṣasya nāradaḥ mokṣam adhyāpayām āsa sāṃkhyajñānam anuttamam
english: Nārada taught Dakṣa's thousand gathered sons the supreme knowledge of liberation, the unsurpassed wisdom of Sāṃkhya.

sanskrit: tataḥ pañcāśataṃ kanyāḥ putrikā abhisaṃdadhe prajāpatiḥ prajā dakṣaḥ sisṛkṣur janamejaya
english: Then Dakṣa the Progenitor, wishing to multiply creation, appointed fifty daughters as his putrikās (daughters treated as sons), O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa kālasya nayane yuktāḥ saptaviṃśatim indave
english: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, twenty-seven suited to the passage of time to Indu (the Moon).

sanskrit: trayodaśānāṃ patnīnāṃ yā tu dākṣāyaṇī varā mārīcaḥ kaśyapas tasyām ādityān samajījanat indrādīn vīryasaṃpannān vivasvantam athāpi ca
english: Of the thirteen wives, the most excellent Dākṣāyaṇī — Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, begat upon her the Ādityas, endowed with might: Indra and the others, and also Vivasvat.

sanskrit: vivasvataḥ suto jajñe yamo vaivasvataḥ prabhuḥ mārtaṇḍaś ca yamasyāpi putro rājann ajāyata
english: From Vivasvat was born the mighty Yama Vaivasvata; and from Yama too, O king, a son was born — Mārtāṇḍa.

sanskrit: mārtaṇḍasya manur dhīmān ajāyata sutaḥ prabhuḥ manor vaṃśo mānavānāṃ tato 'yaṃ prathito 'bhavat brahmakṣatrādayas tasmān manor jātās tu mānavāḥ
english: From Mārtāṇḍa was born the wise and powerful Manu; from Manu this lineage of human beings became celebrated; from Manu were born the Mānavas — brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and the rest.

sanskrit: tatrābhavat tadā rājan brahma kṣatreṇa saṃgatam brāhmaṇā mānavās teṣāṃ sāṅgaṃ vedam adīdharan
english: There, O king, brahminhood was united with the warrior order; those Mānavas who were brāhmaṇas studied the Veda together with its ancillary texts.

sanskrit: venaṃ dhṛṣṇuṃ nariṣyantaṃ nābhāgekṣvākum eva ca karūṣam atha śaryātiṃ tathaivātrāṣṭamīm ilām
english: Vena, Dhṛṣṇu, Nariṣyanta, Nābhāga, Ikṣvāku, Karūṣa, Śaryāti, and also Ilā as the eighth —

sanskrit: pṛṣadhranavamān āhuḥ kṣatradharmaparāyaṇān nābhāgāriṣṭadaśamān manoḥ putrān mahābalān
english: — Pṛṣadhra as the ninth, devoted to the warrior's dharma, and Nābhāgāriṣṭa as the tenth — these are called Manu's mighty sons.

sanskrit: pañcāśataṃ manoḥ putrās tathaivānye 'bhavan kṣitau anyonyabhedāt te sarve vineśur iti naḥ śrutam
english: Fifty more sons of Manu were likewise born on earth; all of them perished through mutual strife — so we have heard.

sanskrit: purūravās tato vidvān ilāyāṃ samapadyata sā vai tasyābhavan mātā pitā ceti hi naḥ śrutam
english: The learned Purūravas was then born from Ilā — she was both his mother and his father, so we have heard.

sanskrit: trayodaśa samudrasya dvīpān aśnan purūravāḥ amānuṣair vṛtaḥ sattvair mānuṣaḥ san mahāyaśāḥ
english: The greatly glorious Purūravas, though human, consumed thirteen islands of the ocean, surrounded by non-human beings.

sanskrit: vipraiḥ sa vigrahaṃ cakre vīryonmattaḥ purūravāḥ jahāra ca sa viprāṇāṃ ratnāny utkrośatām api
english: Purūravas, maddened by his own power, entered into conflict with brāhmaṇas and seized their jewels even as they cried out in protest.

sanskrit: sanatkumāras taṃ rājan brahmalokād upetya ha anudarśayāṃ tataś cakre pratyagṛhṇān na cāpy asau
english: Sanatkumāra, O king, came from the world of Brahman and then counseled him; but he did not accept that counsel.

sanskrit: tato maharṣibhiḥ kruddhaiḥ śaptaḥ sadyo vyanaśyata lobhānvito madabalān naṣṭasaṃjño narādhipaḥ
english: Then that lord of men, overcome by greed, drunk on power, having lost all sense, was immediately cursed by the enraged great sages and perished.

sanskrit: sa hi gandharvalokastha urvaśyā sahito virāṭ ānināya kriyārthe 'gnīn yathāvad vihitāṃs tridhā
english: For he, the sovereign, dwelling in the world of Gandharvas and accompanied by Urvaśī, properly brought the three fires appointed for the rite.

sanskrit: ṣaṭ putrā jajñire 'thailād āyur dhīmān amāvasuḥ dṛḍhāyuś ca vanāyuś ca śrutāyuś corvaśīsutāḥ
english: Six sons were born from Urvaśī: the wise Āyus, Amāvasu, Dṛḍhāyu, Vanāyu, Śrutāyu — sons of Urvaśī.

sanskrit: nahuṣaṃ vṛddhaśarmāṇaṃ rajiṃ rambham anenasam svarbhānavīsutān etān āyoḥ putrān pracakṣate
english: Nahuṣa, Vṛddhaśarman, Raji, Rambha, and Anenas — born of Svarbhānavī — these are declared to be the sons of Āyu.

sanskrit: āyuṣo nahuṣaḥ putro dhīmān satyaparākramaḥ rājyaṃ śaśāsa sumahad dharmeṇa pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: Nahuṣa, son of Āyu, wise and true in valor, ruled a very great kingdom as lord of the earth by the law of righteousness.

sanskrit: pitṝn devān ṛṣīn viprān gandharvoragarākṣasān nahuṣaḥ pālayām āsa brahmakṣatram atho viśaḥ
english: Nahuṣa protected the ancestors, gods, sages, brāhmaṇas, Gandharvas, serpents, Rākṣasas, the priestly order, the warrior order, and the merchant class.

sanskrit: sa hatvā dasyusaṃghātān ṛṣīn karam adāpayat paśuvac caiva tān pṛṣṭhe vāhayām āsa vīryavān
english: Having slain hordes of robbers, the mighty Nahuṣa made sages pay tribute and yoked them to carry him on their backs like beasts of burden.

sanskrit: kārayām āsa cendratvam abhibhūya divaukasaḥ tejasā tapasā caiva vikrameṇaujasā tathā
english: He caused himself to hold the position of Indra, having overpowered the dwellers of heaven by his radiance, austerity, valor, and might.

sanskrit: yatiṃ yayātiṃ saṃyātim āyātiṃ pāñcam uddhavam nahuṣo janayām āsa ṣaṭ putrān priyavāsasi
english: Nahuṣa fathered six sons on his beloved wife: Yati, Yayāti, Saṃyāti, Āyāti, the fifth Uddhava, and a sixth.

sanskrit: yayātir nāhuṣaḥ samrāḍ āsīt satyaparākramaḥ sa pālayām āsa mahīm īje ca vividhaiḥ savaiḥ
english: Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, became emperor, true in his valor; he ruled the earth and performed various sacrifices.

sanskrit: atiśaktyā pitṝn arcan devāṃś ca prayataḥ sadā anvagṛhṇāt prajāḥ sarvā yayātir aparājitaḥ
english: Honoring the ancestors with supreme power and ever reverently worshiping the gods, the unconquered Yayāti bestowed his grace upon all creatures.
